analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow source, patches and metadata against the indexed model and selected T-041 detail. CI's sole change adds the cluster-runtime-models test (.github/workflows/ci.yml:67); surrounding routing, permissions, cache and provider gates are unchanged. Dev release adds two push-trigger paths (release-dev-branch.yml:71-72), without changing branch restrictions, inherited secrets or permissions; its documented branch-review limitation is pre-existing.
release-provider.yml:298-308 adds environment-specific opt-in registration of cluster_runtime. Lines 941-1023 introduce execution of the final bundled app through provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, signing-keychain deletion and identity absence checks, bundle digest verification, and public summary/artifact retention. Lines 1078-1088 require a nonempty facts file when enabled and pass it to publication preparation; facts computation failure is fatal when enabled, advisory otherwise. These changes introduce release-evidence generation, not a visible alteration to inference encryption, tenant cache isolation, billing or serving authorization.
No independently supported regression in this scope. Material integration questions remain for A-011/A-017, TB-011, T-054/T-056: inspect scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py and publication handling to verify sanitized app/worker execution, bounded output, final-byte identity binding and artifact contents. Workflow comments do not prove an empty subprocess environment or that release-reported facts cannot be mistaken for independently approved parity/pair-serving qualifications. Integration must reconcile the coordinator's acceptance/authorization contract without assuming its missing implementation is vulnerable. Also verify that execution of release code cannot expose remaining runner credentials or mutate subsequently published bytes. The supplied release workflow is patch-only; later cleanup/publication interactions are not visible.
